newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex unions study job saving scheme.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex unions study job saving scheme.

text.p: Trade unions at French appliance manufacturer Moulinex are studying a proposal from the company to save 750 jobs by reducing work hours and will pronounce themselves on Monday, a company spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
Moulinex said last June that it wanted to cut 2,600 jobs, 2,100 of them in France, as part of a restructuring aimed at restoring its productivity to the levels of its main rivals.

After an outcry from workers and government officials, Moulinex pledged to try to avoid outright layoffs through early retirement and other plans. One of the plans proposes to save 750 jobs but cutting workers' hours to 1,724 a year from 2,028.

The plan gives workers 33 additional days of leave, but 28 would be set by the company, which would also require workers to accept much more flexibility to take into account the peaks and troughs of annual demand for appliances.
During peak periods, staff would work up to six days a week for a total of 46 hours, but no more than two Saturdays a month.

Moulinex's French workers are represented, in roughly equal parts, by the Force Ouvriere, Socialist-led CFTD, Communist-led CGT, CFTC and the in-house CYDIS unions. Moulinex employs around 11,000 people, most of them in France.
